Connectedness and positive weights force W positive definite on the mean-zero quotient. Euler homogeneity and two-sided fourth-order decrease yield local attraction and Theta(k^-1/2) for every nonzero sufficiently close orbit. Symbolic differentiation verifies the two-color leading scalar -pi^2/2, giving k epsilon_k^2->1/pi^2. Embedded script checks finite graph examples; infinite statements are analytical.

value.rationale: The result resolves the critical upper boundary of a natural graph-parametric family of post-descent period-two orbits: all linearized multipliers equal 1, but a positive-definite quartic forces attraction in every quotient direction with sharp algebraic decay. It yields a topology-independent answer for weighted stars, even cycles, unequal complete bipartite graphs and all connected weighted biregular bipartite networks. The positive quartic mechanism is not a textbook linear stability check and distinguishes nonlinear attraction from both the subcritical hyperbolic window and the supercritical repeller.
